deals.headline: Chelsea owners BlueCo buy 99.7% of RC Strasbourg Alsace
deals.seller: Marc Keller and the club's local shareholders
deals.summary: The club's shareholders agreed to sell to BlueCo, the Chelsea consortium; Marc Keller stayed on as president. Sportune, from the legal filings, puts the price at EUR 4,497.75 per share, i.e. EUR 45m for 100% of the pre-deal capital and EUR 44,986,500 for the 99.7% bought; British press had reported about EUR 75m. BlueCo then lent the club money later converted into equity.

deals.date_text: Budget announced 2 May 2023; works June 2023 to summer 2026
deals.evidence: Le coût des travaux explose et atteint 160 millions d'euros
deals.headline: EUR 160m public-led renovation and extension of the Stade de la Meinau
deals.investor: Eurométropole de Strasbourg with the Ville de Strasbourg, the Collectivité européenne d'Alsace and the Région
deals.summary: The renovation of the Meinau (target capacity 32,000) was budgeted at EUR 160m, split between the city, the Eurométropole (half of the budget), the Collectivité européenne d'Alsace and the Région; the club contributes EUR 9m and pays a higher rent to the Eurométropole. A 35-year occupation agreement was voted on 28 June 2024 and signed on 7 July 2025.

name: Racing Club de Strasbourg Alsace
notes: Revenue is DNCG's total non-transfer earnings for 2024-25 (EUR 38,761k; season played during the Meinau works); net loss EUR -78,305k; DNCG shows net equity of EUR 160,582k at the year end. The SAS files no public accounts beyond the DNCG figures. 2025-26 accounts not yet published. Breakdown uses DNCG categories. Valuation is the 2023 transaction price, not a current market value (Strasbourg is not on the Forbes list). Clearlake's stake in the BlueCo group is shown on Companies House only as a band (more than 50% but less than 75%, 22 Holdco Limited, company 14075518); BlueCo Alsace SAS (SIREN 952912491, president Marc Keller) is registered as Président of the club's SAS. Press reported in August 2026 that Todd Boehly and Mark Walter were negotiating the sale of their BlueCo stakes to Clearlake; not completed in the sources read. Group-level debt (reported Ares facility at 22 Holdco) not verified here and not recorded. No chief executive title: the organigramme lists President Marc Keller and three deputy managing directors (Alain Plet, operations; Matthieu Deroussent, administration & finance; Nicolas Arndt, revenues). Stadium capacity 32,000 is the official project's 2026 target; the club says 2026-27 is the first season after the works. LFP reported Strasbourg's average attendance up 46% in 2025-26, helped by the end of the Meinau works. Social: 3.6m followers across networks at the end of 2025-26 per club data reported by Sportune (27 July 2026), up from 2.018m at the start of the season.

owners.name: BlueCo (BlueCo Alsace SAS; group controlled by Clearlake Capital, with Todd Boehly)

ownership_summary: Since June 2023 the club has belonged to BlueCo, the consortium that bought Chelsea in 2022: its French holding BlueCo Alsace SAS bought 99.7% from Marc Keller and the local shareholders who had owned the club since 2012, at a price equivalent to EUR 45m for 100% of the pre-deal capital (Sportune). BlueCo's UK parent 22 Holdco Limited lists Clearlake Capital's Behdad Eghbali and José E. Feliciano as holding more than 50% but less than 75% of its shares as members of a firm, and Todd Boehly as having significant influence. Marc Keller remains president.
